explanation.surface: A house in the far north has someone living in deep shadow.
explanation.walkthrough: Fitting, since Arctic winters bring long darkness; drop the M from GLOOM.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit dome-shaped shelter built from blocks of snow is a home of the Arctic north.

clue.text: Source of starch fool found in wine

indicators.note: something found in another is inside it

parts.note: cava is Spanish sparkling wine
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A dessert fool has a surprising carb ingredient in its wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool' could be the creamy dessert, which suits the food surface, but it is an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: This tropical root crop yields tapioca, so it is a plant from which starch is obtained.

clue.text: British current design leading to European aircraft

indicators.note: leading to means coming before, so these pieces go in front

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
I is the symbol for electric current
a plan is a design
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A modern British design gives rise to a new European plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like modern, but it is I, the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An early aeroplane with two pairs of wings, one above the other, is a type of flying machine.

clue.text: Support bad English language with feeling?

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
ill means bad, as in ill will
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone defends the use of poor, emotional English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With feeling' suggests emotion, but it means read by touch, and the question mark flags the loose use of 'language'.
explanation.definitionFit: This raised-dot writing system for blind people is read with the fingertips, so it is communicated by touch.

clue.text: Fencing move new in winter sport

indicators.note: something in another is placed inside it

parts.note: the luge is a sled raced feet first
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A fresh manoeuvre appears in a cold-weather sport.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside LUGE after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden forward thrust with the sword, front leg extended, is the basic attacking action of a fencer.

clue.text: Drunken tart kept under observation

parts.note: a tart is a kind of open pie
to eye something is to watch it

explanation.surface: An inebriated woman of loose morals is watched closely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' reads as a woman, but it is a pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal word means very intoxicated, with the glazed look of someone who has had far too much alcohol.

clue.text: So you dated, embracing a lot of fashion again

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: thee is the old-fashioned form of you

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to reform is to form or fashion again

explanation.surface: So you went out with someone, embracing reinvention once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dated' reads as going on dates, but it marks the word as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words introduce a conclusion drawn from what has just been said, meaning consequently or for that reason.
